extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the journal Numerische Mathematik (researchers in numerical mathematics)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, declaring, and submitting manuscripts (including figures, supplementary material, ethical and authorship requirements) to the Springer journal Numerische Mathematik. Intended to ensure submissions meet the journal's technical, ethical, and production standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies that the work described has not been published before and is not under consideration for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission also implies that publication has been approved by all co-authors and the responsible authorities at the institute where the work was carried out; simultaneous submission will be considered a breach of good practice and may result in rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages that have already been published elsewhere must obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) for both print and online formats and include evidence of permission when submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material received without such evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors. Some publishers may charge for electronic rights; Springer cannot refund such costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission file formats and source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should preferably be submitted in the original file format and must include all relevant editable source files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Submit manuscript' link to e-mail the editor and attach files. Failing to submit source files can delay review and production. Provide a PDF of compiled output in addition to source where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page must contain: a concise and informative title; author names; affiliations (institution, (department), city, (state), country); clear indication and active e-mail of corresponding author; ORCID(s) if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If address information is provided with the affiliation it will also be published. For temporarily unaffiliated authors only city and country are captured. Acknowledgments and funding organizations should be placed in a separate section on the title page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Language Models (LLMs) and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT) do not currently satisfy authorship criteria; attribution of authorship carries accountability which cannot be applied to LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of an LLM must be properly documented in the Methods section (or suitable alternative). AI-assisted copy editing (readability/style/error correction) does not need to be declared. In all cases human accountability for the final text is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should not contain undefined abbreviations or unspecified references. (Special life-science trial-registration requirements apply to applicable journals.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 'Statements and Declarations' section in the manuscript containing relevant declarations (e.g., Competing Interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions missing relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete. Refer to submission guideline sections for sample wording and complete the statements appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must disclose financial or non-financial interests directly or indirectly related to the submitted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Competing Interests and Funding' section for details and sample wording; customize statements as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an appropriate number of MSC codes to categorize the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSC codes are used by Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt MATH; refer to www.ams.org/msc for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred manuscript preparation (LaTeX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted in LaTeX and authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include original source (style files and figures) and a PDF. Word files are also accepted but LaTeX is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent hierarchical heading numbering is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Define abbreviations at first mention and use them consistently thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undefined abbreviations in the abstract and elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes may give additional information (including citation of references) but should not consist solely of a reference citation, include bibliographic details, figures, or tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to the text are numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables use superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values). Do not use endnotes — always use footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Place acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc., in a separate section on the title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the names of funding organizations in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical notation conventions (scientific style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard mathematical notation conventions: italic for single-letter variables/constants, roman/upright for numerals, operators, and commonly defined functions, and bold for vectors, tensors, and matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cos, det, e or exp, lim, log, max, min, sin, tan, d (for derivative) in roman/upright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation style in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in the text should be identified by numbers in square brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: [3], [5], [1-3, 7].

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list composition and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference list should include only works cited in the text and be numbered consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal communications and unpublished works should only be mentioned in the text. If available, include DOIs as full DOI links (e.g., 'https://doi.org/abc'). Use standard journal abbreviations per ISSN LTWA or full title if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference entry formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide bibliographic entries in standard formats for journal articles, DOIs, books, book chapters, and online documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are provided for each type (see page). Follow publisher examples for punctuation and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables are to be numbered using Arabic numerals and cited in the text in consecutive numerical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply a table caption explaining components; identify previously published material by a reference at the end of the caption. Use footnote conventions for tables (superscript lower-case letters or asterisks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork and figure submission (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically and indicate what graphics program was used to create each artwork file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name figure files 'Fig' + figure number (e.g., Fig1.eps). Supply editable/vector formats where appropriate and embed fonts in vector graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred figure file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: For vector graphics preferred format is EPS; for halftones (photos) use TIFF; MSOffice files also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector graphics with fonts must have fonts embedded. Scanned line drawings and bitmap line drawings should meet resolution requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Line art (black and white, no shading) should not use faint lines/lettering; all lines at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide; scanned/bitmap line drawings minimum 1200 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure legibility at final size; embed fonts in vector graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone (photograph) resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftone art (photographs/drawings with fine shading) should have a minimum resolution of 300 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If magnification is used include scale bars in the figures themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination art (halftone + line art, extensive lettering, color diagrams) should have a minimum resolution of 600 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable format selection and resolution ensure clarity on publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color art guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free of charge for online publication; ensure main information remains visible in black-and-white print versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If print will be black and white, do not refer to color in captions. Submit color illustrations as RGB (8 bits per channel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sans serif fonts (Helvetica or Arial) for figure lettering and keep lettering consistently sized (about 2–3 mm / 8–12 pt) across final-sized artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize variance of type size within an illustration, avoid effects like shading or outline letters, and do not include titles/captions within illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and part labelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Number all figures using Arabic numerals, cite figures in text in consecutive order, and denote figure parts by lowercase letters (a, b, c...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appendix contains figures continue the consecutive numbering of the main text; figures in online appendices (SI) should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure must have a concise caption describing accurately what the figure depicts; include captions in the text file, not in the figure file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold followed by the figure number in bold; no punctuation after the number or at the end of the caption. Identify all elements found in the figure and cite original sources for previously published material at the end of the caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and size requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Place figures within the body of the text; if file size causes upload problems submit large figures separately. Size figures to fit column width with specified max widths/heights for large and small-sized journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-sized journals: 84 mm (double-column) or 174 mm (single-column) wide, not higher than 234 mm. Small-sized journals: 119 mm wide, not higher than 195 mm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure figures are accessible to people with disabilities: provide descriptive captions, use patterns in addition to colors to convey information, and ensure figure lettering has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive captions enable blind users to access figure content via text-to-speech or Braille hardware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI images policy (figures and SI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must check Springer's policy on generative AI images and ensure adherence to the principles described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies both to figures and supplementary information that include AI-generated images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information (SI) acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer accepts electronic multimedia and other supplementary files to be published online with the article (animations, movies, audio, datasets, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should read the journal's Research data policy before submitting datasets and are encouraged to archive data in repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material file contents and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Include in each supplementary file the article title, journal name, author names, affiliation and e-mail of the corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large file sizes may cause long downloads; consider users' download capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio/Video supplementary technical constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Video aspect ratio: 16:9 or 4:3; maximum file size: 2 GB; minimum duration: 1 sec; supported formats: avi, wmv, mp4, mov, m2p, mp2, mpg, mpeg, flv, mxf, mts, m4v, 3gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure files meet format and size constraints to facilitate online publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text and presentation supplementary formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit text and presentation supplementary material in PDF format; .doc or .ppt are not suitable for long-term viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collection of figures may be combined in a PDF file for SI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spreadsheet supplementary formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Spreadsheets should be submitted as .csv or .xlsx files (MS Excel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard, widely supported formats for long-term accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized file formats allowed for SI
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized formats such as .pdb (chemical), .wrl (VRML), .nb (Mathematica notebook), and .tex can also be supplied as supplementary files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate format and include descriptive caption/content information for each file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining multiple supplementary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple supplementary files may be collected in a .zip or .gz file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name files consecutively (e.g., 'ESM_3.mpg', 'ESM_4.pdf').

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing and naming supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript must make specific mention of supplementary material as a citation (similar to figures and tables). Refer to supplementary files as 'Online Resource N'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure in-text citations to SI are present and consistent with file naming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary captions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each supplementary material supply a concise caption describing the content of the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include captions in the manuscript text; these assist discoverability and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of supplementary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary Information will be published as received from the author without any conversion, editing, or reformatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide SI in the final form intended for publication because no production changes will be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary accessibility (video safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure SI is accessible: manuscript contains descriptive captions; video files must not contain anything that flashes more than three times per second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids risk to users prone to seizures. Also adhere to generative AI image policy where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing services are optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Springer Nature Author Services (language editing, formatting, figure preparation, translation, etc.) is optional and not required for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using services does not imply or guarantee acceptance or selection for peer review. A free Grammar Check tool is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: COPE ethical standards and misconduct handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal follows COPE guidelines to deal with potential acts of misconduct and is committed to integrity of the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of misconduct will be investigated per COPE and may result in rejection, erratum, expression of concern, retraction, or notification of the author's institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and integrity of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be presented clearly, honestly, and without fabrication, falsification or inappropriate data manipulation (including image-based manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should adhere to discipline-specific rules for acquiring, selecting and processing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism prohibition and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: No data, text, or theories by others may be presented as the author's own; proper acknowledgements must be given for copied, summarized or paraphrased material; quotation marks for verbatim copying; permissions for copyrighted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal may use software to screen for plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for software/questionnaires/scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must ensure they have permissions for the use of software, questionnaires/(web) surveys and scales in their studies where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of permissions may invalidate use of the materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate and relevant citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and non-research articles must cite appropriate and relevant literature to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive/inappropriate self-citation or coordinated mutual self-citation is strongly discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of defamatory or untrue statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid untrue statements or allegations about individuals or companies that could be seen as personal attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional tone and factual evidence when discussing entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-use research identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that may be misapplied to pose threats to public health or national security must be clearly identified in the manuscript (dual-use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include creation of harmful agents, disruption of vaccine immunity, chemical hazards, or weaponization of research/technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of supporting documentation/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be prepared upon request to send relevant documentation or data to verify validity of results (raw data, samples, records), excluding sensitive/confidential/proprietary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate documentation to support reproducibility and verification when requested by editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes of misconduct investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: If investigations find valid concerns, outcomes may include manuscript rejection, erratum/correction, expression of concern, retraction, notification of institution, or bibliographic notices regarding peer-review transgressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retractions remain on the platform watermarked 'retracted' with an explanatory note; the reason will be stated in errata/expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of fundamental errors after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an obligation to correct significant errors or inaccuracies discovered post-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the journal, explain how the error impacts the article; remedies may include correction or retraction depending on nature/severity. Retraction notes should transparently indicate impacted parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting or excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals when submitting manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reviewers should be independent and unconnected to the work; provide institutional email or other verifying links/publication record/author ID. Suggest a mix of reviewers from different countries/institutions. Journal may or may not use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship agreement before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must agree with the content and give explicit consent to submit before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher assumes consent and approval from authors and responsible authorities at the institution prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship contribution criteria (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended authorship criteria (adapted from ICMJE): authors listed must have (1) made substantial contributions to conception/design, data acquisition/analysis/interpretation, or creation of new software; (2) drafted or revised critically for important intellectual content; (3) approved the version to be published; and (4) agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher does not strictly prescribe contributions that warrant authorship but recommends adherence to field-specific guidelines; when possible include author contribution statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations content
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information on funding sources, financial/non-financial interests, ethics committee approvals for human/animal research, informed consent for human participants, and animal welfare statements when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which declarations are appropriate to include depending on journal scope and article implications for public health or welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transparency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must ensure data, materials, and software/custom code support published claims and comply with field standards; journals may have individual data-sharing policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible archive research data in repositories in accordance with journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding Author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author who acts on behalf of co-authors and ensures questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring all authors approved the manuscript and order of authors, managing communication with the journal, providing transparency on reuse and unpublished material, and ensuring disclosures/declarations and data statements are included. Managing communication may be delegated but Corresponding Author must be clearly indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution statements (CRediT encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible include contribution statements specifying each author's contributions; CRediT taxonomy examples are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For review articles or thesis-based articles, describe who had the idea, who did the literature search/data analysis, and who drafted/critically revised the work. Place contribution statements on a separate title page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary affiliation should be the institution where the majority of work was done; current addresses may be stated additionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses will not be updated after publication; author names will be published exactly as they appear on the accepted submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the author list, corresponding author, or author order are not accepted after acceptance; adding/deleting authors at revision is generally not permitted but may be warranted in exceptional cases with explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for authorship changes must be explained; approval of such changes during revision is at the Editor-in-Chief's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification (ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to use ORCID IDs when submitting or to acquire one via submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including ORCID helps unambiguously identify authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased or incapacitated authors inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or is incapacitated during the process and co-authors wish to include them, co-authors should obtain approval from a legal representative (e.g., a direct relative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow appropriate legal/ethical procedures for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In authorship disputes during peer review or after publication, the Journal will ask authors to resolve the dispute themselves; if unable, the Journal may withdraw the manuscript or raise the issue with authors' institution(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Journal cannot adjudicate disputes beyond these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal (including correspondence with Editors and reviewers' reports) as confidential unless explicit consent is given to share information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality throughout submission and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-acceptance production steps and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance the article is sent to Production for typesetting; authors will receive e-mails to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights/payment, and a link to proofs once typesetting is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs are for checking typesetting/conversion errors and completeness/accuracy; substantial content changes are not allowed without Editor approval. After online publication further changes can only be made via an Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article publishing agreement and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on journal ownership/policy authors will either grant the Publisher an exclusive licence or transfer copyright to the Publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice (open access) articles do not require transfer of copyright; authors publishing open access agree to publish under a Creative Commons licence; see the journal's How to publish guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints and color print costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints can be ordered by the corresponding author. Online color illustrations are free; color in the print version may require a contribution from authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will be contacted about charges and arrangements after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (hybrid open access) options and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows open access publication in many Springer Nature journals for an Article Processing Charge (APC) which varies by journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include increased access/visibility and easier compliance with funder mandates. APCs and licences offered are listed on the journal's Open access publishing page.
